newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-Aussie scared stiff about job prospects.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Aussie scared stiff about job prospects.

text.p: *AUD holding above the week's 18-month low of $0.7413 but vulnerable after failing to sustain a short covering rally
*Market tense ahead of June jobs data at 11.30 am (0130 GMT)
*Employment gain of less than median 40,250 forecast would be seen as weak and reinforce expectations of rate cut
*Rise above 60,000 needed to curb rate talk and support A$

By 8.00 am (2200 GMT) the currency was fretting at US$0.7443/48 having paced in a US$0.7427/58 range through the night. It finished here at US$0.7435/40 on Wednesday after fading from a US$0.7493 high offshore.

The market was understandably tense about the employment figures given the 40,300 fall in jobs recorded in May had come as a complete shock, knocked more than 1/2 cent off the dollar and had money rates pricing in another official easing.
In this case analysts felt the June result would not be so relevant for policy if in line with forecasts but cautioned against complacency given the notorious volatility of the data.

Median estimates favour a rise in employment of around 40,250 for June, almost exactly correcting May's fall. The unemployment rate was seen edging down to a still high 8.7 percent from 8.8 percent the month before.

The outcome would have to be way outside estimates to alter analysts' thinking on rates, which is that the Reserve Bank would tag any easing to low inflation and avoid the need to use disappointing economic growth as a justification.
It would take an increase of more than 60,000 for the trend in employment growth to pick up even slightly and prompt enough knee-jerk short covering to lift the dollar above 75 cents.

Equally, anything less than a 30,000 gain would be considered weak and an actual fall in employment would have the money market, and the media, howling for an immediate cut in official rates. Such a result would see the dollar testing US$0.7410 again and perhaps down to US$0.7350 by the day's end.
Also out today are private sector credit data for May but these should be lost amid the noise of the jobs figures.

On the crosses the A$ idled at 83.83/93 yen from 83.80/90 late Wednesday. The CRB index recouped a little of its recent steep losses, but any benefit to sentiment was wiped out by a slide in copper to 4-1/2 month lows. -- Wayne Cole 61-29373 1800
